# gstack

gstack turns Claude Code (and other coding agents) into a virtual engineering team: a CEO who rethinks the product, an eng manager who locks architecture, a designer who catches AI slop, a reviewer who finds production bugs, a QA lead who opens a real browser, a security officer who runs OWASP + STRIDE audits, and a release engineer who ships the PR. All slash commands, all Markdown, all free, MIT license.

I'm [Garry Tan](https://x.com/garrytan), President & CEO of [Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/). This is the open source software factory I use every day, and I'm sharing it because these tools should be available to everyone. The story, the productivity numbers and how I run ten sprints at once are in [Why gstack](docs/why-gstack.md).

Fork it. Improve it. Make it yours. And if you want to hate on free open source software — you're welcome to, but I'd rather you just try it first.

**Who this is for:**
- **Founders and CEOs** — especially technical ones who still want to ship
- **First-time Claude Code users** — structured roles instead of a blank prompt
- **Tech leads and staff engineers** — rigorous review, QA, and release automation on every PR

## Quick start

1. Install gstack (two pastes, about 30 seconds of setup; see below).
2. Run `/office-hours` and describe what you're building. It pushes back on your framing and writes a design doc the other skills read.
3. Run `/review` on any branch with changes. It finds the bugs that pass CI but break in production, and fixes the obvious ones.
4. Run `/qa` on your staging URL, or on an isolated local API, CLI, job or webhook. It opens a real browser, reproduces bugs and fixes them.

Stop there. You'll know if this is for you. When you want the whole sprint, `/autoplan` reviews a plan end to end and `/ship` runs tests, review and the PR.

## Install — about 30 seconds

**Requirements:** [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code), [Git](https://git-scm.com/), [Bun](https://bun.sh/) v1.4.2+ (the tested version; setup refuses Bun older than 1.3.3, which would let compiled tools read a project's `.env`), and [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) on Windows. **Recommended on macOS:** the [Aside](https://aside.com) browser (macOS 15+), which the browser skills, `/make-pdf` and `/diagram` drive first with your real logged-in sessions; without it, `./setup` builds gstack's own bundled browser. `/cso` needs a native toolchain as well; setup says so and leaves it unavailable when the toolchain is absent. Timing, the `/cso` prerequisites and the hooks setup registers: [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

### Step 1: Install on your machine

Open Claude Code and paste this. Claude does the rest.

> Install gstack: run **`git clone --single-branch --depth 1 https://github.com/garrytan/gstack.git ~/.claude/skills/gstack && cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup`** then add a "gstack" section to CLAUDE.md that says to use the /browse skill from gstack for all web browsing and never use mcp\_\_claude-in-chrome\_\_\* tools. Claude Code lists the installed skills itself, so the section needs no skill list. Then ask the user if they also want to add gstack to the current project so teammates get it.

**Which updates you get:** a new install follows the `stable` channel, the tagged release (Monday and Thursday at most once every 72 hours, an important fix within about a day, never more than a week stale, plus verified security and regression fixes), instead of every merge to main. `./setup` records this the first time it runs on a machine and prints it. The clone itself starts at main's latest commit, and the updater never moves a checkout backwards, so it moves onto releases at the next cut that passes it (within a few days). A gstack contributor's checkout (marked by `bin/dev-setup`, on a branch other than origin's default `main`, or carrying local commits) and a Capy crew machine (its installer records `main`) follow `main` instead, and an install set up before stable became the default keeps following `main`. To switch, run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config set update_channel main` (every merge) or `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config set update_channel stable` (releases only). Details: [docs/releases.md](docs/releases.md#channels).

### Step 2: Team mode — auto-update for shared repos (recommended)

From inside your repo, paste this. Switches you to team mode, bootstraps the repo so teammates get gstack automatically, and commits the change:

```bash
(cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup --team) && ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-team-init required && git add .claude/ CLAUDE.md && git commit -m "require gstack for AI-assisted work"
```

No vendored files in your repo, no version drift, no manual upgrades. Every Claude Code session starts with a fast auto-update check (throttled to once/hour, network-failure-safe, completely silent). Team mode follows the `stable` channel while `update_channel` is `auto` (so also on an install from before stable became the default): the tagged release (Monday and Thursday at most once every 72 hours, an important fix within about a day, never more than a week stale, plus verified security and regression fixes), not every merge to main. `gstack-config set update_channel main` follows every merge instead; see [docs/releases.md](docs/releases.md#channels).

Swap `required` for `optional` if you'd rather nudge teammates than block them.

Team mode's `required` hook runs on Node.js, so every teammate needs Node.js on PATH ([details](docs/install.md#team-mode)). To remove gstack later: [docs/uninstall.md](docs/uninstall.md).

### Other AI Agents

gstack runs on more agents than Claude. Bare `./setup` installs for Claude
Code only (run inside OpenClaw, Hermes or a Dot, it also registers gstack's
skills with that harness: [docs/hosts.md](docs/hosts.md#agent-harnesses)).
Pick another agent with `--host <name>`, or install for every agent setup
detects on this machine with `--host auto`:

```bash
git clone --single-branch --depth 1 https://github.com/garrytan/gstack.git ~/gstack
cd ~/gstack && ./setup --host auto      # or: ./setup --host codex
./setup --status                         # one row per install: host, tier, scope, version, path
```

An explicit `--host X` installs for X only and never changes another agent's
install. `/gstack-upgrade` refreshes every install it registered, one row per
host, and says which ones failed.

Tiers: **full** is certified by a real workflow run (see
[Certify your host](docs/ADDING_A_HOST.md#certify-your-host)); **experimental**
installs and passes the conformance tests but has no certification run yet;
**instruction-only** installs nothing: setup prints what to copy.

| Agent | Tier | Install | First invocation | Safety skills | Outside review needs | Repair |
|-------|------|---------|------------------|---------------|----------------------|--------|
| Claude Code | full | `--host claude` (default) | `/office-hours` | enforced (hooks block) | Codex CLI, signed in | `./setup --host claude` |
| OpenAI Codex CLI | experimental | `--host codex` → `${CODEX_HOME:-~/.codex}/skills/gstack-*/` | ask for `gstack-office-hours` | advisory, not blocked | Claude Code CLI, signed in | `./setup --host codex` |
| OpenCode | experimental | `--host opencode` → `~/.config/opencode/skills/gstack-*/` + `/gstack-*` commands | `/gstack-office-hours` | advisory, not blocked | Codex CLI, signed in | `./setup --host opencode` |
| Cursor | experimental | `--host cursor` → `~/.cursor/skills/gstack-*/` | ask for `gstack-office-hours` | advisory, not blocked | Codex CLI, signed in | `./setup --host cursor` |
| Factory Droid | experimental | `--host factory` → `~/.factory/skills/gstack-*/` | ask for `gstack-office-hours` | advisory, not blocked | Codex CLI, signed in | `./setup --host factory` |
| Kiro | experimental | `--host kiro` → `~/.kiro/skills/gstack-*/` | ask for `gstack-office-hours` | advisory, not blocked | Codex CLI, signed in | `./setup --host kiro` |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | experimental | `--host copilot` → `~/.copilot/skills/gstack-*/` | `/gstack-office-hours` | advisory, not blocked | Codex CLI, signed in | `./setup --host copilot` |
| Antigravity CLI | experimental | `--host agy` (or `--host antigravity`) → `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/gstack-*/` | `/gstack-office-hours` | advisory, not blocked | Codex CLI, signed in | `./setup --host agy` |
| Gemini CLI | experimental | `--host gemini` (or `--host gemini-cli`) → `~/.gemini/skills/gstack-*/` | ask for `gstack-office-hours` | advisory, not blocked | Codex CLI, signed in | `./setup --host gemini` |
| Slate | instruction-only | `--host slate` (points at the Claude install; Slate reads `.claude/skills`) | `/office-hours` via the Claude install | advisory, not blocked | — | `./setup --host claude` |
| OpenClaw | experimental | `--host openclaw` (five task skills and one `gstack` router skill in OpenClaw's skills folder; automatic when setup runs inside OpenClaw; ACP route in [docs/OPENCLAW.md](docs/OPENCLAW.md)) | ask for the task; the agent opens the matching task skill or the `gstack` router | advisory, not blocked | — | `./setup --host openclaw` |
| Hermes | experimental | `--host hermes` (every skill in `$HERMES_HOME/skills/gstack`; automatic when setup runs inside Hermes) | ask for the task, or `/gstack-review` | advisory, not blocked | — | `./setup --host hermes` |
| GBrain (mod) | instruction-only | `--host gbrain` (brain-aware variants ship from the GBrain repo) | — | advisory, not blocked | — | — |

Per-host notes (agent harnesses, Copilot, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw and ClawHub, the Codex behavioral profile and model tiers, outside-review providers, the design binary's models) are in [docs/hosts.md](docs/hosts.md). Any rules-reading agent (Zed, Amp, Jules) can use the 2KB [agents digest](agents-digest/gstack-AGENTS.md) with no install. Adding a host: [docs/ADDING_A_HOST.md](docs/ADDING_A_HOST.md).

## See it work

```
You:    I want to build a daily briefing app for my calendar.
You:    /office-hours
Claude: [asks about the pain — specific examples, not hypotheticals]

You:    Multiple Google calendars, events with stale info, wrong locations.
        Prep takes forever and the results aren't good enough...

Claude: I'm going to push back on the framing. You said "daily briefing
        app." But what you actually described is a personal chief of
        staff AI.
        [extracts 5 capabilities you didn't realize you were describing]
        [challenges 4 premises — you agree, disagree, or adjust]
        [generates 3 implementation approaches with effort estimates]
        RECOMMENDATION: Ship the narrowest wedge tomorrow, learn from
        real usage. The full vision is a 3-month project — start with
        the daily briefing that actually works.
        [writes design doc → feeds into downstream skills automatically]

You:    /plan-ceo-review
        [reads the design doc, challenges scope, runs 10-section review]

You:    /autoplan
        [eng phase: ASCII diagrams for data flow, state machines, error paths]
        [test matrix, failure modes, security concerns]

You:    Approve plan. Exit plan mode.
        [writes 2,400 lines across 11 files. ~8 minutes.]

You:    /review
        [AUTO-FIXED] 2 issues. [ASK] Race condition → you approve fix.

You:    /qa https://staging.myapp.com
        [opens real browser, clicks through flows, finds and fixes a bug]

You:    /ship
        Tests: 42 → 51 (+9 new). PR: github.com/you/app/pull/42
```

You said "daily briefing app." The agent said "you're building a chief of staff AI" — because it listened to your pain, not your feature request. Eight commands, end to end. That is not a copilot. That is a team.

## The sprint

gstack is a process, not a collection of tools. The skills run in the order a sprint runs:

**Think → Plan → Build → Review → Test → Ship → Reflect**

Each skill feeds into the next. `/office-hours` write

repo.readme:
# agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. - CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors). - A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/quick-start). ## How it works The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each `--session` gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when [session persistence](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions) is configured. Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with `--cdp` or `--auto-connect` ([CDP mode](https://agent-browser.dev/cdp-mode)), select the [Lightpanda](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/lightpanda) or [Obscura](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/obscura) engine with `--engine`, drive Mobile Safari in the [iOS Simulator](https://agent-browser.dev/ios), or use a cloud browser provider such as [Browserbase](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserbase), [Browserless](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserless), [Browser Use](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browser-use), [Kernel](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/kernel), or [AgentCore](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/agentcore). ## For AI agents The CLI ships skills that match its version: ```bash agent-browser skills get core # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows agent-browser skills get core --ref commands # one reference, such as the full command list agent-browser skills get core --full # adds the full command reference and templates agent-browser skills list # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more ``` Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser): ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser ``` The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run `agent-browser skills get core` and follow it. ``` For MCP clients, `agent-browser mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. See [MCP server](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#mcp-server). ## Commands Run `agent-browser --help` for the full list, or `agent-browser --help` for one command. | Group | Commands | Docs | |---|---|---| | Navigate and read | `open`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `read`, `snapshot`, `get`, `is` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Snapshots](https://agent-browser.dev/snapshots) | | Interact | `click`, `dblclick`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `keyboard`, `hover`, `focus`, `select`, `check`, `uncheck`, `scroll`, `drag`, `upload`, `mouse`, `find` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Find elements](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#find-elements) | | Wait | `wait` | [Wait](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#wait) | | Capture | `screenshot`, `pdf`, `record`, `download`, `diff` | [Recording](https://agent-browser.dev/recording), [Diffing](https://agent-browser.dev/diffing), [Files](https://agent-browser.dev/files) | | Page and network state | `cookies`, `storage`, `network`, `set`, `clipboard`, `eval`, `pushstate` | [Network](https://agent-browser.dev/network), [Settings](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#settings) | | Tabs, frames, and dialogs | `tab`, `frame`, `dialog` | [Tabs and frames](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#tabs-frames) | | Debug and performance | `console`, `errors`, `highlight`, `inspect`, `trace`, `profiler`, `vitals`, `react`, `a11y` | [Debugging](https://agent-browser.dev/debugging), [Profiler](https://agent-browser.dev/profiler), [React](https://agent-browser.dev/react) | | Sessions and auth | `session`, `state`, `auth`, `profiles`, `confirm`, `deny` | [Sessions](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions), [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security) | | Agents and integrations | `skills`, `mcp`, `webmcp`, `flow`, `chat`, `batch`, `plugin` | [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/skills), [WebMCP](https://agent-browser.dev/webmcp), [Plugins](https://agent-browser.dev/plugins) | | Observe | `stream`, `dashboard` | [Streaming](https://agent-browser.dev/streaming), [Dashboard](https://agent-browser.dev/dashboard) | | Setup | `install`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `connect`, `close` | [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation) | Flags, environment variables, and `agent-browser.json` are documented in [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration). ## Platforms Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host. ## Development Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust: ```bash pnpm install pnpm build:source # builds the dashboard and the native CLI pnpm link --global agent-browser install ``` Run the Rust checks from `cli/`: ```bash cargo fmt -- --check cargo clippy cargo test cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1 # launches real headless Chrome ``` [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process. ## Documentation - [agent-browser.dev](https://agent-browser.dev): introduction, guides, and reference - [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/commands) and [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration) - [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security): the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries - [Next.js and Vercel](https://agent-browser.dev/next) and [eve](https://agent-browser.dev/eve): running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## License Apache-2.0

repo.readme:
Any Cloud. Locally.
Light, fluffy, and always free
No account. No auth token. No feature gates. Just docker compose up.

Quick Start · Features · Services · SDKs · Testcontainers · Migration · Docs

--- ## What is Floci? Floci is a free, open-source local AWS emulator for development, testing, and CI. It gives you AWS-shaped services on your machine without requiring a cloud account, an auth token, or paid feature gates. Point your AWS SDK, CLI, Terraform, CDK, OpenTofu, or test suite at `http://localhost:4566` and keep your existing workflows. Already using LocalStack? Floci is a drop-in replacement: swap the image and keep going. See [Migrating from LocalStack](#migrating-from-localstack). Floci is the AWS member of the [Floci](https://github.com/floci-io) emulator family, named after [floccus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirrocumulus_floccus), the cloud formation that looks like popcorn. | Emulator | Cloud | Port | |---|---|:---:| | **[floci](https://github.com/floci-io/floci)** | **AWS** | **4566** | | [floci-az](https://github.com/floci-io/floci-az) | Azure | 4577 | | [floci-gcp](https://github.com/floci-io/floci-gcp) | GCP | 4588 | | [floci-oci](https://github.com/floci-io/floci-oci) | OCI | 4599 | ## Quick Start The fastest way to run Floci is with the official [CLI](https://github.com/floci-io/floci-cli) ```bash floci start ``` No Docker? Each [release](https://github.com/floci-io/floci/releases) also ships a standalone `floci-aws` binary for Linux, macOS and Windows; see [Native binary](https://floci.io/floci/getting-started/installation/#native-binary). Export the AWS environment variables: ```bash eval $(floci env) ``` Use your existing AWS tools normally: ```bash aws s3 mb s3://my-bucket aws dynamodb create-table \ --table-name demo-table \ --attribute-definitions AttributeName=pk,AttributeType=S \ --key-schema AttributeName=pk,KeyType=HASH \ --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST aws dynamodb list-tables ``` ### Watch it run This short demo shows the CLI flow: start Floci, export the local AWS environment, run standard AWS CLI commands, and stop the emulator. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b55714dc-ef36-40ae-a734-cd2cadc288a8 All AWS services are available at `http://localhost:4566`. Any [published AWS region](https://floci.io/floci/configuration/partitions/) works, in every partition. Credentials can be any non-empty values unless you explicitly enable stricter service-specific auth checks.
Prefer Docker Compose? Create a `compose.yaml` file: ```yaml services: floci: image: floci/floci:latest ports: - "4566:4566" ``` Start Floci: ```bash docker compose up ``` Then configure your AWS environment manually: ```bash export AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localhost:4566 export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1 export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=test export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=test ```
Using the old hectorvent/floci image? Update your image name: ```yaml # Before image: hectorvent/floci:latest # After image: floci/floci:latest ``` The old `hectorvent/floci` repository no longer receives updates.
## Web Console Floci ships a browser console for inspecting the resources in your local emulator. **Open it at:** `http://localhost:4566/_floci/ui` Nothing runs at boot. The first request pulls the console image, starts it as a sidecar container on Floci's Docker network, hands it Floci's own reachable address plus the standard AWS environment, polls its health endpoint, and redirects the browser once it reports it can reach Floci. The sidecar's port is bound by Docker, so it needs no `ports:` entry of your own, and its logs are streamed into CloudWatch Logs under `/floci/ui`. Starting a container needs the Docker socket: ```yaml services: floci: image: floci/floci:latest ports: - "4566:4566" volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock ``` | Variable | Default | Description | |---|---|---| | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_ENABLED` | `true` | Enable the console sidecar | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_IMAGE` | `floci/floci-ui:0.7.0` | Console image to run | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_CONTAINER_NAME` | `floci-ui` | Name of the sidecar container | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_PORT` | `4500` | Host port the console is published on | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_BIND_ADDRESS` | _(none)_ | Host interface that port is published on. Unset publishes on every interface; set `127.0.0.1` when Floci's own port is loopback-only | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_KEEP_RUNNING_ON_SHUTDOWN` | `false` | Leave the sidecar running when Floci stops | ### Running a different console The console is not fixed to the one Floci ships. Any console implementing the [Floci console contract](https://floci.io/floci/ui/console-contract/) runs with nothing but an image name: listen on the port in `PORT`, serve `GET /api/health`, talk to Floci at `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`. ```yaml environment: FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_IMAGE: acme/my-console:1.0 ``` A console that differs from the contract's defaults says so in its own `io.floci.console.*` image labels, so its operators do not have to. [StackPort](https://github.com/DaviReisVieira/stackport), for example, listens on 8080 rather than 4500; on an image that predates the labels, say it by hand: ```yaml environment: FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_IMAGE: davireis/stackport:latest FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_CONTAINER_NAME: floci-stackport FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_PORT: "8080" FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_INTERNAL_PORT: "8080" ``` [Floci Dash](https://github.com/ofsazib/floci-dash) is another. It honours `PORT`, so only the two things it does differ on need naming: ```yaml environment: FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_IMAGE: ghcr.io/ofsazib/floci-dash:latest FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_CONTAINER_NAME: floci-dash FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_ENDPOINT_ENV: FLOCI_URL FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_STATUS_PATH: /api/healthz ``` The endpoint itself is never configured by hand: Floci resolves its own reachable address at start time and injects it as `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`. Full reference: [Web Console](https://floci.io/floci/ui/) and [Console Contract v1](https://floci.io/floci/ui/console-contract/). ## Features
Local AWS without the cloud account Run AWS-compatible services locally without an AWS account, auth token, or paid feature gates.
Real Docker where fidelity matters Lambda, RDS, Neptune, ElastiCache, MSK, ECS, EC2, EKS, OpenSearch, CodeBuild, and Managed Service for Apache Flink use real Docker-backed execution instead of shallow mocks.
Drop-in AWS compatibility Point standard AWS clients at `http://localhost:4566`. Existing credentials, regions, SDKs, CLI commands, and IaC workflows stay familiar. Terraform can provision AWS-shaped resources locally through Floci using the standard HashiCorp AWS provider. See the [Terraform with Floci guide](docs/getting-started/terraform.md) for provider configuration, resource examples, and optional emulated S3 state.
Fast enough for CI The native image starts in milliseconds and keeps idle memory low, making it practical for local development and test pipelines.

# agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree.

agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output, and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop status # platform, permissions, supported surfaces agent-desktop permissions --guide # macOS: walks you through the Accessibility grant ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable. On macOS and Linux, Homebrew also works: `brew install agent-desktop`. There is no official Scoop package yet. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. Release archives and building from source are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify ``` Each command prints one JSON envelope. A trimmed snapshot: ```json { "version": "2.6", "ok": true, "command": "snapshot", "data": { "app": "Finder", "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9", "ref_count": 59, "complete": true, "tree": { "role": "window", "name": "Downloads", "children": [ { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] } ] } } } ``` - **Refs belong to their snapshot.** A bare `@e8` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS`. When the UI changes, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: take a new snapshot and use its refs. - **Several windows** give `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`; `snapshot` lists the candidate window ids in `error.details`. Pass one with `--window-id`. - **Dense apps:** map first with `snapshot --skeleton --app Slack -i --compact`, then drill into one region with `snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact`. - **Headless by default.** Ref actions use the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus. The global `--headed` flag allows physical input. - **Post-action waits** observe the ref's original process. Window-owned refs stay pinned to their original window, including refs captured from a sheet, alert, popover, focused view, or Linux menu. macOS application menus keep their application-owned surface and need no document window. The wait reads the whole pinned window, so overlay selectors share its scope. [Wait scope and results](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/configuration#post-action-wait-flags) describe the selector limits. - `type`, `set-value`, and `clipboard-set` accept `--stdin` for piped text, keeping it out of process arguments. Run secret steps as separate commands; batch JSON text appears in process arguments. - **PowerShell.** Quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e8'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/quick-start). ## How it works Your agent calls the CLI, or the C library in process. Both run the same core, which reaches the OS only through `PlatformAdapter`. Each binary is built for one OS and talks to that OS's accessibility API. ## For AI agents The binary carries guides that match its version: ```bash agent-desktop skills get desktop # the loop, refs, verification and retry rules agent-desktop skills get platform # what differs on the OS you run on agent-desktop --help # flags for one command ``` Install the skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/agent-desktop): ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop ``` Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-desktop` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run `agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them. ``` Retry a failed command only when `error.disposition.retry` is `safe`. See [JSON output](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/json-output) for the envelope, error codes, and exit codes. ### MCP `agent-desktop mcp` serves every command as an MCP tool over stdio. A tool is named after its command (`desktop_snapshot`, `desktop_click`, `desktop_session_start`), takes that command's arguments, and returns its JSON envelope: ```json { "mcpServers": { "agent-desktop": { "command": "agent-desktop", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` Global flags given to `mcp`, such as `--session`, `--headed` or `--trace`, apply to every call. ## Commands agent-desktop has 60 command names, 56 operational commands. The other four (`key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up`) refuse to run until a daemon can release a held key or button. [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/commands) documents each one. | Group | Commands | |---|---| | Observe | `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` | | Act on a ref | `click`, `double-click`, `triple-click`, `right-click`, `type`, `set-value`, `clear`, `focus`, `select`, `toggle`, `check`, `uncheck`, `expand`, `collapse`, `scroll`, `scroll-to` | | Keyboard and mouse | `press`, `hover`, `drag`, `mouse-move`, `mouse-click`, `mouse-wheel`, `key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up` | | Apps and windows | `launch`, `close-app`, `list-apps`, `list-windows`, `list-displays`, `focus-window`, `resize-window`, `move-window`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `restore`, `open-system-surface` | | Notifications | `list-notifications`, `dismiss-notification`, `dismiss-all-notifications`, `notification-action` | | Clipboard | `clipboard-get`, `clipboard-set`, `clipboard-clear` | | Wait | `wait` | | Sessions | `session`, `trace`, `cursor-overlay` | | System | `status`, `permissions`, `version`, `batch`, `skills` | ## Platform support | Platform | Requirement | Accessibility API | |---|---|---| | [macOS](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/macos) | macOS 13 or later, Intel or Apple Silicon | AX API | | [Windows](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/windows) | Windows 10 1809 or later, x64 or ARM64 | UI Automation | | [Linux](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/linux) | Ubuntu 24.04 or later, x86_64 or aarch64, X11 or Wayland | AT-SPI | Each platform page lists what works headless, what needs `--headed`, and what refuses. ## C library Each release ships `libagent_desktop_ffi`, so a program can call agent-desktop in process. See the [C library docs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/ffi). ```python import ctypes lib = ctypes.CDLL("./lib/libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib") lib.ad_adapter_create.restype = ctypes.c_void_p lib.ad_adapter_destroy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p] assert lib.ad_init(7) == 0 # AD_RESULT_OK when the header's AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR matches the library adapter = lib.ad_adapter_create() lib.ad_adapter_destroy(adapter) ``` ## Development Each platform adapter builds only on its own OS, so scope cargo to the host's packages. On macOS: ```bash HOST_PKGS=(-p agent-desktop-core -p agent-desktop-macos -p agent-desktop -p agent-desktop-ffi) cargo test "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" cargo clippy "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings ``` On Windows, use `agent-desktop-windows` instead of `agent-desktop-macos`; on Linux, `agent-desktop-linux`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) lists every gate. ## Documentation - [Introduction](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop): what it is and how it works - [Snapshots and refs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/snapshots-and-refs) - [Errors and recovery](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/errors-and-recovery) - [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/skills) - [CONCEPTS.md](CONCEPTS.md): vocabulary - [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md) ## License Apache-2.0

Build with a spec, fix a bug, or assess an idea — with your coding agent.

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

Spec Kit is an open source toolkit that gives AI coding agents structured processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes. Start with a ready-made process, customize it, or bring your own. ## Choose your process | What you need | Process | Outcome | | --- | --- | --- | | Build a feature or application | [Spec-Driven Development](#spec-driven-development) | A specification carried through planning, implementation, and convergence | | Diagnose and repair broken behavior | [Bug fixing](#bug-fixing) | An assessed cause, scoped fix, and recorded verification | | Decide whether an idea deserves investment | [Idea assessment](#idea-assessment) | An evidence-backed go, clarify, or stop decision | | Adopt or create a different process | [Your own process](#capabilities) | A process adapted or assembled from reusable primitives | These are independent entry points, not mandatory phases. SDD ships in core; bug fixing and assessment are bundled extensions you install when needed, and the primitives below let you adopt or create other processes. ## Capabilities Spec Kit combines ready-to-use processes with composable mechanisms: | Capability | Spec Kit mechanism | | --- | --- | | Connect to or switch between coding agents | [Integration](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/index.html) | | Add a command, quality gate, or complete process | [Extension](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/overview.html) | | Connect a process to an external tool or service | [Extension](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/overview.html) | | React to coding-agent lifecycle events | [Extension runtime catalogs](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/install/air-gapped.html) | | Inspect which layer supplies a command, template, or script | [Artifact and `specify bundle search`. Spec Kit includes community catalogs, and organizations can add their own curated sources. Catalog listings are not audits or endorsements, so review community source code before installing or running it. ## Get started You need Python 3.11+, [uv](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/install/uv.html), and a supported AI coding agent on Linux, macOS, or Windows. Run these commands in your terminal to install Spec Kit and create a project. This example uses GitHub Copilot. ```bash uv tool install specify-cli specify init my-project --integration copilot cd my-project ``` After installing the Specify CLI and creating your project, launch your coding agent in the project directory, then choose a process below. For other setups: - [Installation](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/installation.html) for pinned releases, other installers, CI, and troubleshooting. - [Existing projects](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/existing-projects.html) to start with code you already have. - [Other agents](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/index.html) for integration keys and [invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation). - [Upgrade](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/upgrade.html) to update an existing installation. ## Spec-Driven Development Define what to build and why, then turn the specification into a plan, tasks, and working code. Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing. This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. The final verdict is `verified`, `partial`, or `failed`; only `verified` confirms a successful fix. [Bug-fixing walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/bugfix.html) · [Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-bugfix.html) ## Idea assessment Gather evidence to decide whether an idea is worth pursuing. This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. Resolve unknowns by editing the existing Markdown artifacts, directly or with your agent, rather than rerunning whole stages. If you choose to build a software idea with a `go` decision, establish a project constitution if needed, then pass the handoff summary from `decision.md` to `/speckit-specify`. # Skills For Real Engineers [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/mattpocock/skills)](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy. If you want to keep up with changes to these skills, and any new ones I create, you can join ~60,000 other devs on my newsletter: [Sign Up To The Newsletter](https://www.aihero.dev/s/skills-newsletter) ## Installation (30-second setup) A plugin updates itself. [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) copies editable files into your project, and you update them by hand. Pick one per agent, because installing both gives you every skill twice. ### 1. Get the skills
Claude Code ```bash claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official ``` Updates itself by default.
Codex ```bash codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Updates itself at startup.
GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code) ```bash copilot plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills copilot plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Then, once, add to `~/.copilot/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "mattpocock": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "mattpocock/skills" }, "autoUpdate": true } } } ``` In VS Code, run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source** and enter `https://github.com/mattpocock/skills`. It updates daily.
Gemini CLI (manual updates) ```bash gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/engineering gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/productivity ``` Re-run both commands to update.
Any other agent, or editable files (manual updates) ```bash npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a # cursor, opencode, devin, windsurf, amp, pi; omit -a to choose ``` When the installer asks which skills to take, include `setup-matt-pocock-skills`. To update, run `npx skills@latest update`, and re-run `add` to pick up new skills.
### 2. Run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` In your agent, run it once per repo. It will: - Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, GitLab, local files, or anything else you describe) - Ask you what labels you apply to tickets when you triage them (`/triage` uses labels) - Ask you where you want to save any docs we create ### 3. Bam - you're ready to go. ## Why These Skills Exist I built these skills as a way to fix common failure modes I see with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents. ### #1: The Agent Didn't Do What I Want > "No-one knows exactly what they want" > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**. The most common failure mode in software development is misalignment. You think the dev knows what you want. Then you see what they've built - and you realize it didn't understand you at all. This is just the same in the AI age. There is a communication gap between you and the agent. The fix for this is a **grilling session** - getting the agent to ask you detailed questions about what you're building. **The Fix** is to use: - [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md) - for non-code uses - [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md) - same as [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md), but adds more goodies (see below) These are my most popular skills. They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them _every_ time you want to make a change. ### #2: The Agent Is Way Too Verbose > With a ubiquitous language, conversations among developers and expressions of the code are all derived from the same domain model. > > Eric Evans, [Domain-Driven-Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Domain-Driven-Design-Tackling-Complexity-Software/dp/0321125215) **The Problem**: At the start of a project, devs and the people they're building the software for (the domain experts) are usually speaking different languages. I felt the same tension with my agents. Agents are usually dropped into a project and asked to figure out the jargon as they go. So they use 20 words where 1 will do. **The Fix** for this is a shared language. It's a document that helps agents decode the jargon used in the project.
Example Here's an example [glossary](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/blob/076a5a7a182db0fe1e62971dd7a68bcadf010f1c/CONTEXT.md) (still named `CONTEXT.md` at that pinned commit, from before the skills renamed the convention), from my `course-video-manager` repo. Which one is easier to read? - **BEFORE**: "There's a problem when a lesson inside a section of a course is made 'real' (i.e. given a spot in the file system)" - **AFTER**: "There's a problem with the materialization cascade" This concision pays off session after session.
This is built into [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md). It's a grilling session, but that helps you build a shared language with the AI, and document hard-to-explain decisions in ADR's. It's hard to explain how powerful this is. It might be the single coolest technique in this repo. Try it, and see. > [!TIP] > A shared language has many other benefits than reducing verbosity: > > - **Variables, functions and files are named consistently**, using the shared language > - As a result, the **codebase is easier to navigate** for the agent > - The agent also **spends fewer tokens on thinking**, because it has access to a more concise language ### #3: The Code Doesn't Work > "Always take small, deliberate steps. The rate of feedback is your speed limit. Never take on a task that’s too big." > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**: Let's say that you and the agent are aligned on what to build. What happens when the agent _still_ produces crap? It's time to look at your feedback loops. Without feedback on how the code it produces actually runs, the agent will be flying blind. **The Fix**: You need the usual tranche of feedback loops: static types, browser access, and automated tests. For automated tests, a red-green-refactor loop is critical. This is where the agent writes a failing test first, then fixes the test. This helps give the agent a consistent level of feedback that results in far better code. I've built a **[`/tdd`](./skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md) skill** you can slot into any project. It encourages red-green-refactor and gives the agent plenty of guidance on what makes good and bad tests. For debugging, I've also built a **[`/diagnosing-bugs`](./skills/engineering/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md)** skill that wraps best debugging practices into a disciplined loop, gated phase by phase. ### #4: We Built A Ball Of Mud > "Invest in the design of the system _every day_." > > Kent Beck, [Extreme Programming Explained](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Extreme-Programming-Explained-Embrace-Change/dp/0321278658) > "The best modules are deep. They allow a lot of functionality to be accessed through a simple interface." > > John Ousterhout, [A Philosophy Of Software Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Philosophy-Software-Design-2nd/dp/173210221X) **The Problem**: Most apps built with agents are complex and hard to change. Because agents can radically speed up coding, they also accelerate software entropy. Codebases get more complex at an unprecedented rate. **The Fix** for this is a radical new approach to AI-powered development: caring about the design of the code. This is built in to every layer of these skills: - [`/to-spec`](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md) quizzes you about which modules you're touching before creating a spec And crucially, [`/improve-codebase-architecture`](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md) surveys a codebase for deepening opportunities and hands you the candidates. I recommend running it on your codebase once every few days. It is a survey, not a rescue: on a genuinely old codebase it will find real candidates, but it won't untangle the mud for you. ### Summary Software engineering fundamentals matter more than ever. These skills are my best effort at condensing these fundamentals into repeatable practices, to help you ship the best apps of your career. Enjoy. ## Reference These split on one axis: who can invoke them. **User-invoked** skills are reachable only when you type them (e.g. `/grill-me`); their job is to orchestrate. **Model-invoked** skills can be invoked by you _or_ reached for automatically by the agent when the task fits; they hold the reusable discipline. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, but never another user-invoked one. ### Engineering Skills I use daily for code work. **User-invoked** - **[ask-matt](./skills/engineering/ask-matt/SKILL.md)**: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the user-invoked skills in this repo. - **[grill-with-docs](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md)**: Grilling session that also builds your project's domain model, sharpening terminology and updating `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs inline. - **[triage](./skills/engineering/triage/SKILL.md)**: Move issues through a state machine of triage roles. - **[improve-codebase-architecture](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md)**: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick. - **[setup-matt-pocock-skills](./skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md)**: Configure this repo for the engineering skills (issue tracker, triage labels, domain doc layout). Run once per repo before using the other engineering skills. - **[to-spec](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md)**: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker. No interview, just synthesizes what you've already discussed. - **[to-tickets](./skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md)**: Break any plan, spec, or conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, written as text in a local file, or as native blocking links on a real tracker. - **[implement](./skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md)**: Build the work described by a spec or set of tickets, driving `/tdd` at pre-agreed seams and closing out with `/code-review` before committing. - **[implement-spec](./skills/engineering/implement-spec/SKILL.md)**: Implement a whole spec on one integration branch. 全能的光盘盘面可见图像生成与刻录工具

Disc Image Studio 是一个多平台的光盘盘面图像生成与刻录工具，帮助您使用任何刻录光驱在任何 DVD / CD / 单层蓝光 光盘上刻蚀出肉眼可见的图像。 ![.NET 版本](https://img.shields.io/badge/.NET-10.0-512bd4?style=flat-square) ![运行平台](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20macOS-0078d6?style=flat-square) ![开发语言](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-C%23-68217A?style=flat-square) ![GitHub Repo size](https://img.shields.io/github/repo-size/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio?style=flat-square&color=3cb371) ![贡献欢迎](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-Welcome-brightgreen?style=flat-square) [![许可证：GPL-3.0-or-later](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL--3.0--or--later-blue?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)
--- ## 效果预览 ![](docs/images/case1.jpg) ![](docs/images/case2.jpg) --- ## 概述 Disc Image Studio 可将一张图片转换成符合 CD、DVD 与单层 BD-R 光盘物理层约束的数据，刻录后将使光盘盘面呈现肉眼可见的图案。 ## 界面预览 ![主页：模板与最近工程](docs/images/ui-home.png) ![设计页：图层画布与影调](docs/images/ui-design.png) ![导出页：浅色主题与输出镜像](docs/images/ui-export.png) --- ## 快速开始 Windows 下载 `win-x64.exe` 后可直接运行。Linux 或 macOS 请下载与 CPU 匹配的**实验性 CLI** 压缩包，解压后运行 `./disc-image-studio --help`。这些发布包均自带 .NET 运行时。 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/releases) ### 1. 新建工程 在主页选择 CD、DVD 或蓝光，指定输出位置后创建工程。 ### 2. 设计盘面 在设计页导入图片，用图层完成排版，并在右栏「影调」模块调整抖动、伽马、亮度与灰阶档位。 ### 3. 预览与导出 在预览页核对盘面投影，在导出页生成 ISO / RAW / WAV+CUE，或使用即时刻录功能直接写入空白盘片。 即时刻录为实验性功能，请只使用可报废的测试介质。 ## 功能 ### 光盘数据生成 - **CD 支持**：支持任何 CD 。您可导出带格式头的 WAV 音轨及配套 CUE，兼容 cdrecord, ImgBurn等刻录软件；也允许导出 RAW 音轨。详见 [CD 刻录兼容说明](docs/CD_AUDIO_COMPATIBILITY.md)。 - **DVD 支持**：支持任何 DVD。您可导出 ISO 镜像。 - **蓝光支持**：支持任何单层 BD-R 25 GB，支持纯绘图与 UDF 2.01 文件。详见 [ADDING_BLURAY.md](docs/ADDING_BLURAY.md)。 - **随盘文件**：CD／DVD／蓝光可在设计页直接选择要保存的文件夹及内圈／外圈位置，也可在导出页调整；设置随工程保存。 - **文件区域预览**：混合盘的设计投影和成品读回用黄色标出文件区（含文件系统）。 - **介质灰度方案**：CD 与 DVD 均使用黑白二阶，CD 使用 `0D / AA`，DVD 扰码域使用 `A5 / 92`。详见 [PHYSICAL_MODEL_AUDIT.md](docs/PHYSICAL_MODEL_AUDIT.md)。 - **灰度抖动工具**：独立程序也可将原图处理为 `0/255` 黑白二阶 PNG；支持打开或拖入原图、并排预览及无损 PNG 导出。详见[使用与构建说明](tools/FourLevelDither/README.md)。 - **盘片预设**：内置数个品牌的光盘参数，覆盖 CD／DVD／BD。您也可将自己标定好的数据贡献给我们，详见[预设维护说明](docs/DISC_PRESETS.md)。 ### 辅助标定 Disc Image Studio 提供粗标定、边界标定和精细标定流程，通过盘面照片估计内外半径与轨距分布。下面的历史实盘对比中，校准前采用恒定轨距，十字线的径向线条出现明显弯曲；使用辅助标定得到的三次轨距参数重新生成并刻录后，线条更接近径向直线。实测精度取决于照片矫正、取点和复刻验证，参数保存的小数位数不代表测量精度。 | 校准前 · 恒定轨距 | 校准后 · 三次轨距 | | --- | --- | | ![校准前的 DVD 实拍：径向十字线明显弯曲](docs/images/verbatim-dvd-calibration-before.jpg) | ![校准后的 DVD 实拍：径向十字线更接近直线](docs/images/verbatim-dvd-calibration-after.jpg) | | `P20261004-133519.jpg` | `P20261004-135416.jpg` | 第一次使用可跟随[DVD 标定实操教程：Verbatim AZO DVD-R](docs/CALIBRATION_TUTORIAL.md)，查看照片矫正、三个标定阶段的实际取点、参数变化与参考值，以及精标后的盘面效果。完整流程与参数说明见[辅助标定说明](docs/CALIBRATION.md)。 ### 刻录 - **镜像文件输出**：您可以导出完整 ISO / RAW 文件并使用合适的刻录软件手动刻录。 - **即时流式刻录（实验性）**：CD、DVD 与 BD-R 边生成边刻录，不保存完整镜像；BD-R 走 MMC 顺序写入。 - **不要使用非空白介质！** ## 系统与设备要求 - 桌面版需要 Windows 10 2004（2004/20H1，19041）及以上，或 Windows 11。 - 构建：.NET 10 SDK（`global.json` 锁定 10.0.x）；自行构建的非自包含 GUI 需要 .NET 10 Windows 桌面运行时。Release EXE 已包含运行时，无需另行安装 .NET。 - “即时刻录”功能需要一台 Windows 可识别的 CD / DVD / BD 刻录机与空白盘片；BD-R 需要支持顺序写入的单层空白盘。 ## 构建与运行 ```powershell dotnet build DiscImageStudio.slnx --configuration Release dotnet run --project src/DiscImageStudio.App --configuration Release ``` 构建回归检查： ```powershell dotnet run --project src/DvdImageSolver --configuration Release -- selftest dotnet run --project tests/DiscImageStudio.ArchitectureTests --configuration Release ``` 版本规则、CI 生成 EXE、Release 草稿检查、MSIX 打包与签名流程见[发布指南](docs/RELEASING.md)。 ## 命令行 Linux（glibc）可选 `linux-x64` 或 `linux-arm64`。Apple Silicon Mac 选 `osx-arm64`，Intel Mac 选 `osx-x64`。CLI 在本地生成镜像，实际写盘可交给支持相应镜像或音轨的刻录软件。 使用 .NET 10 SDK 从源码运行 CLI ```sh dotnet run --project src/DiscImageStudio.Cli -c Release -- --help ``` CLI 可读取 PNG、JPEG、BMP 和 GIF，使用动画图片的第一帧。下面的例子用两扇区音轨验证安装，同时生成配套 CUE。 ```sh ./disc-image-studio cd-generate --input picture.png --output sample.wav --sectors 2 ``` | 命令 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | `solve` | 使用固定快速纹理映射（CW 方向）生成 DVD 镜像，黑白纹理可选抖动混合 | | `encode` | 将单个 DVD ECC 块编码为 NRZI 通道电平 | | `calibrate` | 标定投影：按生成几何从 DVD 源图片取样，按实测几何投到盘面 | | `simulate` | 按实测半径对生成的 DVD ISO 做读回模拟 | | `selftest` | 运行 DVD 引擎的确定性回归自检 | | `cd-generate` | 无随盘文件时生成 WAV + CUE / RAW 音轨；指定 `--data-dir` 时生成 CD 数据盘 ISO | | `cd-preview-warp` | 标定投影：按实测几何投影 CD 源图片 | | `cd-preview-track` | 按标定几何渲染已有的 WAV 或 RAW CD-DA 音轨（读回模拟） | | `bd-generate` | 生成完整 BD-R ISO，并写出 `.json` sidecar | | `bd-info` / `bd-probe` / `bd-encode` | 导出 BD 参数、原始负载探针或单个 ECC 簇诊断 | 各命令的完整参数见对应文档。 ## 源码结构 ```text src/DiscImageStudio.Cli/ Linux 和 macOS 离线命令行入口 src/DiscImageStudio.ImageIO/ WIC 和跨平台图像编解码 src/DiscImageStudio.Core/ 介质无关的模块契约、工程/预设模型、任务与命令目录 src/DiscImageStudio.Imaging/ CD/DVD/BD 共用的图片预处理与抖动辅助 src/DiscImageStudio.Burning/ Windows IMAPI2 设备枚举、流缓冲与安全刻录层 src/DiscImageStudio.Cd/ CD-DA 生成核心与 CD 模块 src/DiscImageStudio.Dvd/ DVD 引擎适配模块 src/DiscImageStudio.BluRay/ BD-R 几何、17PP/ECC、3T/6T 映射、流式生成与 ISO src/DiscImageStudio.Iso/ UDF 2.01 / ISO9660 写入器 src/DiscImageStudio.App/ WPF GUI、统一命令行与商店资源 src/DvdImageSolver/ 保持隔离的 DVD 编码/求解引擎 tests/ 无第三方测试框架的架构回归测试 packaging/ MSIX 清单与打包脚本 tools/ 独立辅助工具与资产生成脚本 docs/ 架构、引擎、预设、发布等文档 ``` ## 参考标准 Disc Image Studio 的实现与物理模型主要参考以下规范： | 介质 | 标准与版本 | 本项目采用的范围 | | --- | --- | --- | | CD-R | [ECMA-394，第 1 版，2010 年 12 月](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-394/) — *Recordable Compact Disc Systems CD-R Multi-Speed*（[官方 PDF](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-394_1st_edition_december_2010.pdf)） | CD-R 介质、多速录制及 CD-DA 兼容关系；本项目生成 CD-DA 音轨。 | | DVD 公共格式 / DVD-ROM | [ECMA-267，第 3 版，2001 年 4 月](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-267/) — *120 mm DVD – Read-only disk*（[官方 PDF](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-267_3rd_edition_april_2001.pdf)） | DVD 数据帧、ECC、EFMPlus 编码及附录 G 转换表；可记录盘的介质规则另参考 ECMA-359。 | | DVD-R | [ECMA-359，第 1 版，2004 年 12 月](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-359/) — *80 mm (1,46 Gbytes per side) and 120 mm (4,70 Gbytes per side) DVD Recordable Disk (DVD-R)*（[官方 PDF](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-359_1st_edition_december_2004.pdf)） | 单层 DVD-R 的几何、扇区、纠错和编码；标准包含单面及双面介质，双面不等于双层。 | | BD-R | [ISO/IEC 30190:2021，第 3 版，2021 年 1 月](https://www.iso.org/standard/80770.html) — 120 mm 单层（25.0 GB）及双层（50.0 GB）可记录 BD 的信息交换与存储规范 | 实验模式采用单层 25 GB 的轨道、扇区布局、纠错和编码；目前不支持双层盘。 | CD 公共编码部分还参考了 [ECMA-130，第 2 版（CD-ROM，1996）](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-130/)。 ## 刻录与介质安全须知 - Disc Image Studio 不安装驱动或服务；“即时刻录”功能使用了 Windows 自带的 IMAPI2，拒绝非空白介质。 - “即时刻录”功能已有部分实盘反馈，对不同设备、介质与刻录入口的验证覆盖仍有限，属于实验性功能，请只使用可报废的测试介质。刻录中断、断电或生成速度不足仍可能使盘片报废！ - 实际可见效果取决于盘片、刻录机、固件与写入策略。 - 混合文件夹会在开始刻录前扫描目录并固定布局；期间源文件大小改变会安全终止任务，已开始写入的盘片仍可能报废。 - BD-R 顺序写入不提供备用区重映射；中断后同一盘片通常不能继续写入。 ## 隐私与安全 - Disc Image Studio 不联网、不上传文件、不收集遥测，详见[隐私政策](PRIVACY.md)。 - 发现安全问题请不要在公开 Issue 中披露，按[安全政策](SECURITY.md)使用 GitHub 私密报告。 ## 贡献 欢迎报告问题与提交代码。开发环境搭建、模块边界规则、测试要求与 Pull Request 流程见[贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING.md)。 ## 许可证 项目采用 [GNU GPL v3.0 or later](LICENSE)（`GPL-3.0-or-later`）。CD 交织实现包含从 CDImage 移植并修改的代码，整体分发沿用兼容的 GPL 授权；分发二进制或修改版时须遵守对应源代码等要求。第三方字体与组件遵循各自许可证，详见 [授权说明](LICENSE-NOTICE.md) 和 [第三方声明](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt)；应用"关于"页也可离线查看完整文本。 ## 致谢 感谢 [arduinocelentano 的 CDImage 项目](https://github.com/arduinocelentano/cdimage)，它展示了通过生成 CD 音轨在盘面形成可见图像的方法。本项目的 CD 交织实现由其相关代码移植并继续修改，CD 盘面绘图思路也受其启发。CDImage 原作者及贡献者的工作为本项目提供了重要基础。 --- ## Star History
